items.title: Henry "Jack" Palmer Interview
items.q: I didn't know Robert Junior that day when you started. No. Robert Junior wasn't even talking about, did you?

ctx.x: Well, I'm going to tell you. I didn't know too much about. I know the guitar players. I'm going to tell you about the guitar players. The only guitar players I have in there. What's that bright boy's name, man? What's that bright boy named Walter? What used to? Willoughby? Was that his name? Willoughby? Yeah. Willoughby? Now, wait a minute. Him and Buddy Doris. Guitar players in the car. How do you know what? What's that? I'm saying. I'm on the drum. I don't know what I'm about. That's Willoughby. Guitar players.…
Robert Junior wasn't even talking about, did you?

You wasn't talking about. Willoughby. Buddy Doris. And, uh, and Blind Boy fellow. And, uh, who else was there? We always used horns. Yeah. Trumpets. In that time, you played by yourself mostly. Little local fellows. Yes. Fellows like a band. You know how the band. And, uh, you know. Well, I mean, I had to go out to play for a day. And for some. I had trampone and sax. Drums. Yeah, I never did have upright bass. Them were drums. Oh. I played there in Chicago. Fifteen years. Trill. Which he got there. And take the…

items.title: Henry "Jack" Palmer Interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...if you put you up there, you'd play with Robert Jr., Jim Tucker, anybody else...

ctx.x: See, the thing about you, if you put you up there, you'd play with Robert Jr., Jim Tucker, anybody else, you see. See, and what they was playing, that's like a Hatchet called playing with Memphis Mini. He would sound like a fool playing with Memphis Mini, you understand what I mean? Because he was way over that kind of music.
